source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enable HTTP BOOT on onboard NIC. Verify HTTP boot function from each NIC port.
1. In BIOS setup, verify that all the HTTP BOOT enabled NICs/LOMs show up in the boot sequence.
2. With on board NIC cards enabled, reboot the server and choose the HTTP BOOT option.
3. Select the NIC port from the list for HTTP BOOT boot.
4. Download efi from http server successfully.
5. Boot into grub.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. On board NIC ports should be shown in the boot sequence page when HTTP BOOT function is enabled

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- HTTP BOOT function test (IPv4): HTTP BOOT IPv4 boot test needs the operator to enable HTTP BOOT in BIOS, reboot, choose the HTTP BOOT option, download the efi from the HTTP server and boot into grub - a BIOS/boot-menu interactive flow the agent cannot drive from the OS.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator enables HTTP BOOT in BIOS, selects the option per NIC port, downloads the efi and boots into grub; agent cannot drive the pre-OS HTTP boot menu.

original_test_intent: Verify that each approved onboard NIC presents an IPv4 HTTP Boot firmware entry, downloads the exact approved EFI artifact and hands control to GRUB.
original_method: An operator enables and selects each firmware HTTP Boot entry and observes download/GRUB handoff; the agent validates the fixed artifact and correlates HTTP request logs by port/MAC before settings restoration.
manual_activity: Firmware entry observation, per-port selection and confirmation that the EFI reaches GRUB are operator-controlled acceptance steps; automation supplies server and artifact evidence only.
required_inputs: Isolated IPv4 HTTP Boot server and fixed URL
Console/BMC access, reboot approval and firmware restore plan
safety_requirements: Isolate the HTTP boot service and pin URL, artifact identity and checksum.
Do not equate HTTP 200, OS NIC visibility or a server request with firmware/GRUB success.
Record and restore boot order and HTTP Boot settings.
Stop on wrong artifact, ambiguous port, unexpected boot target, unisolated service or console loss; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Validate server readiness and artifact hash; collect request status, bytes, client/MAC correlation and supporting OS/BMC health.
Prepare a per-port evidence table without operating the pre-OS UI or deciding PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Enable HTTP Boot, inspect each firmware entry, select each port and attest EFI download and GRUB handoff.
Restore settings and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The narrative correctly says the agent cannot drive the flow; no executable substitute proves the firmware/GRUB criterion.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use project-approved read-only NIC inventory, artifact hashing and HTTP access logs as supporting evidence keyed to operator timestamps and MAC/port.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The per-port IPv4 HTTP/EFI/GRUB scope and 40/40-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture the firmware entry and GRUB handoff on console while correlating the selected NIC to a fixed URL, exact EFI checksum and HTTP transfer record.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Servers with UEFI IPv4 HTTP Boot support.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS/BMC, NIC firmware, HTTP server, EFI and GRUB versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform UEFI HTTP Boot documentation and approved boot-artifact manifest.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds artifact identity, per-port correlation, isolation and restoration evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Distinguishes correct firmware boot of the approved image from a generic HTTP response or wrong-file transfer.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: NIC map, URL, artifact hash and expected GRUB state.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Server logs cannot prove firmware UI presentation or GRUB display; those remain manual.

project_override_considerations: Projects may select ports, URL and EFI image, but the report must bind results to the exact hash and cannot claim coverage for untested ports or images.
expected_evidence: NIC/MAC/port map, isolated server readiness and artifact hash
Operator firmware-entry and per-port selection captures
HTTP request/response/byte record correlated to client and approved artifact
Restored boot/HTTP state and health logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Items and Procedure consistently define IPv4 HTTP Boot through EFI download and GRUB; the shorter Criteria covers firmware entry visibility but does not contradict the additional source steps.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The operator-executable flow is clear; its acceptance-critical pre-OS observations make it MANUAL ONLY rather than blocked.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains the correct manual boundary and adds artifact and server evidence controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps its per-port, checksum, isolation and restoration improvements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates agent support, manual execution and engineer verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents a request for the wrong EFI or an HTTP 200 response from being reported as proof of a successful approved firmware-to-GRUB boot.
independent_technical_reasoning: HTTP Boot success spans firmware menu presentation, NIC selection, exact object retrieval and EFI/GRUB execution; server automation can prove the transfer but not the pre-OS selection or handoff display.
